title: closing-bible inspection (inspection.json)
description: PRD §4 'Version selection' and 'Execution evidence': for each family, the proposed selected source, a structured execution finding, the missing components, and the evidence — matching execution pages, date, version marker, completeness, checklist reference and hash. Written by the skill after it has looked at the documents; validated by the reconciliation script before anything is counted. Anything outside this shape, or a proposed_status the findings do not support (status-taxonomy.md 'Derivation'), is rejected with a named reason. Inspection proposes; reconciliation and the user decide.

corpus_id.description: Must equal the manifest's corpus_id; an inspection of a different folder is refused.

member_ids.description: Must equal the family's members in families.json.

proposed_pick.description: The member proposed as the final version. null when proposed_status is version-conflict or unreadable.

proposed_status.description: Must equal the status the derivation table produces from execution, execution_expected and missing_components; otherwise the record is rejected.

execution_expected.description: Whether the parties sign this document (agreement, deed, certificate) rather than it being a schedule, filing receipt or unsigned exhibit. When a checklist supplies this, the checklist wins.

referenced_at.description: Where the reference was seen: a clause, a contents page, or a checklist row.

execution_finding.description: PRD §4 'Execution evidence' (without a ledger, render and inspect the execution pages: appears signed / appears incomplete / unclear) and 'Execution spotlight' (apparent document date, signature-page locations). This is what the no-ledger path populates the index and overview from. When a current sigpack ledger covers the pick, reconciliation overrides these from the ledger (rule 4).

apparent_status.description: not-expected when execution_expected is false; not-inspected when the pages could not be looked at (say why in note).

document_date.description: The date as printed on the execution page, verbatim. Never from a filename or timestamp (rule 3).

source.description: sigpack-ledger and visual-inspection are the only sources that may support an execution or date claim (status-taxonomy.md rule 1).

locator.description: Page, ledger page id (e.g. SPA-p13) or filename — precise enough for the lawyer to look at the same thing.

observation.description: What was seen. 'Seller block carries a signature and printed name.' Never 'validly executed'.
